_note: GRAVITY WELLS - entity `gravity_agent` / `gravity_agent.ent`, the role table's
`gravity_well`. Ten placements across five levels, and the last mechanic in the game
that is not a boss.
A well is THREE things at once, and a port that builds only the first would leave five
levels looking finished and playing wrong:
1. a SOLID CIRCLE. The node is a StaticBody2D with a CircleShape2D, so the agent is an
obstacle in its own right and a portal shot already dies on it (Shot::FirstBody
walks sphere colliders and skips only triggers). That part the port already had.
2. an ATTRACTOR. Every dynamic body inside its radius is pulled toward the centre.
3. a NO-PORTAL ZONE. ETHCallback_gravity_agent ADDS an antiportal.ent at its own
position on its first tick, so no portal may be placed inside the well's reach.
The third is the one that is invisible from the level file: nothing in the .tscn says
`antiportal`. It exists only in the callback.
ETHCallback_gravity_area (bytes 461443..462571), over the dynamic bodies near it -
DynamicBodyChooser::choose rejects IsStatic() and anything with no physics controller,
so platforms and walls sit still inside a well and only loose bodies move:
forceDir  = normalize(thisPos - bodyPos)          // TOWARD the centre: it attracts
inRange   = squaredDist < squaredRadius
forceBias = smoothEnd(1 - squaredDist/squaredRadius)
fpsFix    = lastFrameElapsedMs / 16.6666
force     = scale(forceDir * forceBias * forceLength * fpsFix)
SetLinearVelocity(GetLinearVelocity() + force)
ADDED, never set - the same idiom as the portal recoil (zerog.json) and for the same
reason: a body falling into a well keeps the speed it arrived with.
THE OPERAND ORDER WAS CHECKED, because it is the whole difference between a well and a
fan. vector2::opSub is called with thisPos as the OBJECT and bodyPos as the argument,
so the direction runs from the body to the centre. It pulls in.
TWO STRENGTHS, and the branch is on the WORLD's gravity: GetGravity() == V2_ZERO gives
0.18, anything else 0.5. That splits these five levels exactly - level16c, level17c and
level18c are no_gravity levels and pull at 0.18; level20c and level27c have the world's
gravity and pull at 0.5. The stronger pull is in the levels where gravity is already
fighting it, which is why the port reads Game::Level::noGravity rather than asking the
registry what its PhysicsSettings say.
THE UNITS NEED NO CONVERSION, for the reason zerog.json sets out at length: the same
scale() wrapper wraps the world's gravity as scale(10), and Units.hpp has that 10
decoded as Box2D's DEFAULT_GRAVITY in metres per second squared. So 0.18 and 0.5 are
metres per second, added once per reference frame. At 60 fps fpsFix is ~1, so a body at
the very centre gains about 10.8 m/s^2 in a zero-gravity level - about one gravity -
and 30 m/s^2 in a level that has its own.
smoothEnd(v) IS sin(v * PIb). PIb is a global the decoder renders by name and never
defines - every one of its appearances is a use, so this is INFERRED and not decoded:
PI/2, from three independent uses. As `sin(v * PIb)` it is an ease-out that must reach
1.0 at v = 1; `PI + PIb` appears as a half-turn plus a quarter; and getAngle brackets
its quadrant tests with `PIb / 2` and `PI + PIb / 2`. All three are PI/2 and nothing
else. Said plainly here because a data file that calls an inference a decode is worse
than one that admits the gap.
The antiportal the agent adds is sized by scaleToSize(area, vector2(w, h)) with
w = h = radius*2 - scale(24). scaleToSize reads GetSize() and calls Scale(size /
currentSize), so that width and height are the ENTITY'S SIZE - not a radius.
And an antiportal refuses a tap within GetSize().x * 0.5, which is what the port's
placement.json decodes as antiportalRadiusPx. So the well's no-portal RADIUS is
(radius*2 - 24) / 2  =  radius - 12
and NOT the radius itself. Twelve pixels, at every one of the ten placements. The
shrink is carried here as the size it is, and halved where it is used, so that the
arithmetic in the code reads the way the original's does.
This is also why the port's existing antiportalRadiusPx CANNOT serve. That is a
constant 64 times the node's own scale - half of white_ring.png's 128 px frame - and
these zones run from 52 to 248 px. Portals::NoPortalZone gains an explicit radius for
them, defaulting to the old arithmetic so every antiportal already in the game is
untouched.
Measured by reading every metadata/radius in chapter 4, NOT by counting grep lines.
TEN placements across FIVE levels:
level16c  106
level20c  260
level27c  128
A CORRECTION, recorded because it nearly became a documented fact. test_mp_zerog
printed `8 gravity wells across 3 of the eighteen`, and that is right for what it
measured - it walks the eighteen zero-gravity levels only, so level20c and level27c
were never in its loop. The game-wide total is ten across five.
level20c's 260 px is wider than most rooms in the game are tall; whatever else that
level is about, the well dominates it.
